parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A solid cylinder of weight $24\text{ N}$ is made of material of density $850\text{ kg m}^{-3}$. The cylinder has a length of $0.18\text{ m}$, as shown in Fig. 1.1.
{{figure:figure_1_1}}
Fig. 1.1
Show that the cross-sectional area $A$ of the cylinder is $0.016\text{ m}^2$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
The cylinder in (a) is attached by a spring to the bottom of a rigid container of liquid, as shown in Fig. 1.2.
{{figure:figure_1_2}}
Fig. 1.2 (not to scale)
The cylinder is in equilibrium with its bottom face at a depth of $0.17\text{ m}$ below the surface of the liquid. The tension in the spring is $8.0\text{ N}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Show that the upthrust acting on the cylinder due to the liquid is $32\text{ N}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the density of the liquid.

parts.label: (c)
(c)(i)
parts.text:
The tap at the bottom of the container is opened so that a fixed amount of liquid flows out of the container. The cylinder moves downwards so that the tension in the spring changes from $8.0\text{ N}$ to $4.0\text{ N}$.
Determine the change in the elastic potential energy of the spring.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
More liquid is let out of the container until the upthrust on the cylinder becomes $24\text{ N}$.
For the upthrust of $24\text{ N}$, determine the length of the spring.
